acceptance.reason: tests/test_pipeline.py::test_order_and_cleanup returns [True, 5, 5] for SET/INCR/GET and leaves p.commands == [] and p.watched == set(); independent fake-connection diagnostics also confirmed ordering/return values and cleanup on success, including a watched success path.

Injected first-GET failure in SET(x,1)->GET(x)->GET(y): one reconnect and only the failed GET was replayed (calls SET,GET,GET,GET), confirmed SET ran once and results were [True,1,None]; a second consecutive failure produced exactly two attempts, one reconnect, then ConnectionError. A failure after two confirmed SETs retried only the failed GET.

With a watch registered, injected connection loss raised WatchError, reconnects == 0, and the call log contained no replay (SET once, failing GET attempted once); with a confirmed prefix the watched loss still raised WatchError and did not replay the failed command; commands and watched state were cleared.

Injected loss on INCR with an unknown outcome raised WatchError, INCR was sent exactly once, no reconnect/replay occurred and the store was not double-incremented; INCR-first and safe-command-with-unconfirmed-INCR-suffix variants also raised WatchError without replay. A confirmed INCR prefix was not re-executed when a later safe command was retried.

After success, after watched WatchError, and after non-idempotent-unknown WatchError, p.commands == [] and p.watched == set(); the same pipeline then executed new commands with correct results in all cases. Cleanup also held for an unexpected connection exception and for a reconnect failure.

requestReview.reason: The original request requires safe reconnect and cleanup, preserving GET/SET/INCR/WATCH, never replaying watched work or work with an unknown non-idempotent outcome (report WatchError), retrying safe unwatched work at most once from the failed command without repeating a confirmed prefix, and clearing queued commands and watch state on every exit. brief.md and specs/pipeline/spec.md restate these constraints without scope reduction, and the implementation/tests match: GET and SET are replay-safe, INCR is not, watched loss raises WatchError, confirmed prefixes are not re-executed, and a finally block clears both command and watch state on all exits.

acceptance.reason: Independent read-only execution: set('a',4).incr('a').get('a').execute() returned [True, 5, 5] in order; commands and watched were empty after success; a second get('a').execute() on the same pipeline returned [5] and cleared state again. Runtime check normal-operations (python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -q) passed with 2 tests, exit 0, bound to the current candidate input gate.

Independent read-only execution with a connection dropping on the second command, after a confirmed SET: execute() returned [True, 7], the call log was [SET a 7, GET a, GET a] (confirmed SET sent once, failed GET retried once), and reconnect count was 1. A two-command confirmed prefix was likewise not repeated, and two consecutive drops on a safe GET stopped after one retry (two total attempts). Runtime normal-operations tests passed.

Independent read-only execution: with watch('k').get('k') and the next connection call failing, execute() returned [None] instead of raising WatchError and the call log shows [GET k, GET k], so the watched operation was replayed. With watch('k').set('k',1), execute() returned [True] and the call log shows [SET k 1, SET k 1] with store {'k': 1}, replaying a watched mutation. Cause: redis_like/pipeline.py:37 clears self.watched before redis_like/pipeline.py:38 tests self.watched, making the watched-loss WatchError branch unreachable.

Independent read-only execution: with the next connection call failing, incr('k').execute() raised WatchError('operation outcome is unknown'), the call log contained exactly one INCR, and the key was absent from the store. A mid-pipeline INCR after a confirmed SET likewise raised WatchError after the SET, was not re-executed, and left the confirmed SET value intact.

The original request explicitly requires that a watched operation is never replayed after connection loss and that WatchError is reported.
